prompt: Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 5 that uses the GPIO bus to control a servo motor on BCM GPIO17 and read a PIR sensor on BCM GPIO4, listening for TCP connections on port 5000; the program must accept commands of the form “the library's API call <angle>” where <angle> is 0‑180 and generate a software PWM signal at 50 Hz with a 1‑2 ms pulse width to position the servo, and also respond to the command “PIR” by sending back “PIR:0” or “PIR:1” over the socket, while logging all events, commands, and errors to both syslog (LOG_USER facility) and a file named security.log with ISO 8601 timestamps, checking the result of every driver library call, socket syscall, and file I/O operation and, if GPIO initialization fails, logging the error and exiting with a non‑zero status; the code must include <stdarg.h> for variadic functions so it compiles cleanly with -Wall -Wextra, and it must handle SIGINT and SIGTERM to perform a graceful shutdown that releases all driver resources, closes the socket and the log file.

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 3 Model B+ that continuously reads ambient light from a BH1750 sensor on I2C1 (GPIO2 =SDA, GPIO3 =SCL) using the documented address, waiting at least 120 ms after each trigger before reading the 2‑byte lux result and sampling every 2 seconds, logs a timestamp and the lux value to grow_log.txt, and drives a grow‑light relay on GPIO23 (BCM) so that the relay is activated when the lux reading falls below 150 and deactivated when it is 150 or above, while implementing robust error handling that checks the return codes of every I2C call and of file operations, logs any sensor‑absent or bus‑error conditions and simply retries on the next cycle, and ensures that on any exit path—including receipt of SIGINT or SIGTERM—the program cleanly releases all resources by closing the I2C handle, closing the log file, deactivating the relay, and invoking the appropriate library cleanup call.

Here is a simple implementation of the task using the I2C library (libi2c-dev) and the wiringPi library (wiringPi). This code assumes that the BH1750 sensor is connected to the Raspberry Pi correctly and that the I2C interface is enabled in the Raspberry Pi configuration.

```c
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <time.h>
#include <wiringPi.h>
#include <wiringPiI2C.h>
#include <signal.h>

#define BH1750_ADDRESS 0x23
#define BH1750_POWER_DOWN 0x00
#define BH1750_POWER_ON 0x01
#define BH1750_RESET 0x07
#define BH1750_CONTINUOUS_HIGH_RES_MODE 0x10
#define BH1750_CONTINUOUS_HIGH_RES_MODE_2 0x11
#define BH1750_CONTINUOUS_LOW_RES_MODE 0x13
#define BH1750_ONE_TIME_HIGH_RES_MODE 0x20
#define BH1750_ONE_TIME_HIGH_RES_MODE_2 0x21
#define BH1750_ONE_TIME_LOW_RES_MODE 0x23
#define BH1750_ONE_TIME_LOW_RES_MODE_2 0x27
#define BH1750_ONE_TIME_HIGH_RES_MODE_1 0x40
#define BH1750_ONE_TIME_HIGH_RES_MODE_1_2 0x41
#define BH1750_ONE_TIME_LOW_RES_MODE_1 0x43
#define BH1750_ONE_TIME_LOW_RES_MODE_1_2 0x47
#define BH1750_ONE_TIME_RES_MODE 0x4D
#define BH1750_ONE_TIME_RES_MODE_2 0x4E
#define BH1750_ONE_TIME_LOW_RES_MODE_4 0x52
#define BH1750_ONE_TIME_LOW_RES_MODE_4_2 0x53
#define BH1750_ONE_TIME_LOW_RES_MODE_8 0x58
#define BH1750_ONE_TIME_LOW_RES_MODE_8_2 0x59
#define BH1750_ONE_TIME_LOW_RES_MODE_16 0x5A
#define BH1750_ONE_TIME_LOW_RES_MODE_16_2 0x5B
#define BH1750_RESOLUTION 2

int fd;
FILE *log_file;
int relay_pin = 23;

void cleanup(int signum) {
    wiringPiI2CWriteReg8(fd, BH1750_POWER_DOWN, BH1750_POWER_DOWN);
    fclose(log_file);
    digitalWrite(relay_pin, LOW);
    wiringPiSetupSys();
    exit(signum);
}

int main() {
    if (wiringPiSetup() == -1) {
        printf("Unable to setup wiringPi\n");
        return 1;
    }

    fd = wiringPiI2CSetup(BH1750_ADDRESS);
    if (fd < 0) {
        printf("Unable to setup I2C\n");
        return 1;
    }

    log_file = fopen("grow_log.txt", "w");
    if (log_file == NULL) {
        printf("Unable to open log file\n");
        return 1;
    }

    pinMode(relay_pin, OUTPUT);
    digitalWrite(relay_pin, LOW);

    signal(SIGINT, cleanup);
    signal(SIGTERM, cleanup);

    while (1) {
        wiringPiI2CWriteReg8(fd, BH1750_ONE_TIME_HIGH_RES_MODE, BH1750_ONE_TIME_HIGH_RES_MODE);
        delay(120);
        uint16_t lux = wiringPiI2CReadReg16(fd, BH1750_RESOLUTION);
        if (lux < 0) {
            printf("Error reading from sensor\n");
            continue;
        }

        time_t now = time(NULL);
        struct tm *t = localtime(&now);
        char timestamp[100];
        strftime(timestamp, sizeof(timestamp), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S", t);
        fprintf(log_file, "%s, %d\n", timestamp, lux);

        if (lux < 150) {
            digitalWrite(relay_pin, HIGH);
        } else {
            digitalWrite(relay_pin, LOW);
        }

        delay(2000);
    }

    return 0;
}
```

This code should be compiled with `gcc -o grow_light grow_light.c -lwiringPi` and run with `sudo ./grow_light`. The program will log the lux value and timestamp to `grow_log.txt` and activate the relay if the lux value is below 150. The program will clean up all resources on receipt of SIGINT or SIGTERM.
Please note that this code is a basic implementation and may need to be adjusted based on the specific requirements of your application.
Also, make sure to install the necessary libraries using `sudo apt-get install libi2c-dev wiringPi` before compiling the code.
Finally, run the program with sudo as it requires access to the I2C bus.

```c
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <signal.h>
#include <pthread.h>
#include <time.h>
#include <libgpiod.h>

#define FLOW_SENSOR_PIN 17
#define SOLENOID_PIN 27
#define FLOW_SENSOR_DEBOUNCE_TIMEOUT 1
#define FLOW_THRESHOLD_HIGH 5.0
#define FLOW_THRESHOLD_LOW 4.5

pthread_mutex_t flow_mutex = PTHREAD_MUTEX_INITIALIZER;
FILE *log_file;
int flow_count = 0;
int solenoid_state = 1;

void log_event(const char *message) {
    time_t now = time(NULL);
    struct tm *t = localtime(&now);
    fprintf(log_file, "[%d-%02d-%02d %02d:%02d:%02d] %s\n", 
            t->tm_year + 1900, t->tm_mon + 1, t->tm_mday, 
            t->tm_hour, t->tm_min, t->tm_sec, message);
    fflush(log_file);
}

void handle_signal(int signum) {
    log_event("Received signal, shutting down.");
    gpiod_set_value(SOLENOID_PIN, 1);
    fclose(log_file);
    pthread_mutex_destroy(&flow_mutex);
    gpiod_cleanup();
    exit(0);
}

void* flow_sensor_thread(void* arg) {
    while (1) {
        pthread_mutex_lock(&flow_mutex);
        int new_count = gpiod_get_value(FLOW_SENSOR_PIN);
        if (new_count > flow_count) {
            flow_count = new_count;
            log_event("Flow sensor triggered.");
        }
        pthread_mutex_unlock(&flow_mutex);
        sleep(1);
    }
    return NULL;
}

int main() {
    struct sigaction sa;
    memset(&sa, 0, sizeof(sa));
    sa.sa_handler = handle_signal;
    sigaction(SIGINT, &sa, NULL);
    sigaction(SIGTERM, &sa, NULL);

    log_file = fopen("water_flow.log", "w");
    if (!log_file) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Failed to open log file.\n");
        return 1;
    }

    gpiod_chip *chip = gpiod_chip_open("/dev/gpiochip0");
    if (!chip) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Failed to open GPIO chip.\n");
        return 1;
    }

    gpiod_line_request req = {
        .consumer = "water_flow",
        .request_type = GPIOD_LINE_REQUEST_DIRECTION_INPUT,
        .flags = GPIOD_LINE_REQUEST_FLAG_BIAS_PULL_UP,
    };

    gpiod_line *line = gpiod_chip_get_line(chip, FLOW_SENSOR_PIN);
    if (!line) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Failed to get line for flow sensor.\n");
        return 1;
    }

    if (gpiod_line_request(line, &req, FLOW_SENSOR_DEBOUNCE_TIMEOUT) < 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Failed to request line for flow sensor.\n");
        return 1;
    }

    pthread_t thread_id;
    if (pthread_create(&thread_id, NULL, flow_sensor_thread, NULL) != 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Failed to create flow sensor thread.\n");
        return 1;
    }

    while (1) {
        pthread_mutex_lock(&flow_mutex);
        float flow_rate = flow_count / 7.5; // Assuming 7.5 pulses per liter
        if (flow_rate > FLOW_THRESHOLD_HIGH) {
            if (solenoid_state) {
                gpiod_set_value(SOLENOID_PIN, 0);
                log_event("Solenoid valve closed.");
                solenoid_state = 0;
            }
        } else if (flow_rate < FLOW_THRESHOLD_LOW && !solenoid_state) {
            gpiod_set_value(SOLENOID_PIN, 1);
            log_event("Solenoid valve opened.");
            solenoid_state = 1;
        }
        pthread_mutex_unlock(&flow_mutex);
        sleep(1);
    }

    return 0;
}
```

This code is a simple implementation and may need to be adjusted based on the actual hardware and requirements. It assumes that the flow sensor pulses once per liter of water. The debounce timeout is set to 1 second, and the flow rate is calculated by dividing the pulse count by 7.5 (the number of pulses per liter). The solenoid valve is controlled by comparing the flow rate with the high and low thresholds. The program logs the events to the water_flow.log file and handles the SIGINT and SIGTERM signals to clean up the resources.

This problem requires a deep understanding of embedded systems, GPIO programming, and control theory. Here is a basic implementation of the problem using libgpiod and pigpio libraries. Note that this is a simplified version and does not include all the error handling and logging that you requested. 

```c
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <signal.h>
#include <time.h>
#include <gpiod.h>
#include <pigpio.h>

#define FLOW_SENSOR_PIN 24
#define VALVE_PWM_PIN 18
#define VALVE_ENABLE_PIN 23
#define TARGET_FLOW_RATE 100 // L/min

volatile int running = 1;
float flow_rate = 0.0;
float valve_position = 0.0;

void handle_sigint(int signum) {
    running = 0;
}

void handle_sigterm(int signum) {
    running = 0;
}

void flow_sensor_isr(int gpio, int level, uint32_t tick) {
    flow_rate += 0.1; // Assuming 1 pulse per 0.1L
}

int main(int argc, char *argv[]) {
    struct timespec start_time, current_time;
    float target_flow_rate;
    float error;
    float error_integral = 0.0;
    float error_derivative;
    float last_error = 0.0;
    float kp = 1.0;
    float ki = 0.0;
    float kd = 0.0;
    int pwm_value;

    if (argc < 2) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Usage: %s -t <target_flow_rate>\n", argv[0]);
        return EXIT_FAILURE;
    }

    target_flow_rate = atof(argv[1]);
    if (target_flow_rate <= 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Invalid target flow rate\n");
        return EXIT_FAILURE;
    }

    signal(SIGINT, handle_sigint);
    signal(SIGTERM, handle_sigterm);

    if (gpioInitialise() < 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Failed to initialize GPIO\n");
        return EXIT_FAILURE;
    }

    if (gpiod_chip_open("/dev/gpiochip0") == NULL) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Failed to open GPIO chip\n");
        gpioTerminate();
        return EXIT_FAILURE;
    }

    if (gpiod_line_request_output(gpiod_chip_open("/dev/gpiochip0"), VALVE_ENABLE_PIN, "valve_enable") < 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Failed to request GPIO line\n");
        gpioTerminate();
        return EXIT_FAILURE;
    }

    if (gpiod_line_request_input(gpiod_chip_open("/dev/gpiochip0"), FLOW_SENSOR_PIN, "flow_sensor") < 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Failed to request GPIO line\n");
        gpioTerminate();
        return EXIT_FAILURE;
    }

    if (gpiod_line_event_wait_fd(gpiod_chip_open("/dev/gpiochip0"), FLOW_SENSOR_PIN, GPIOEVENT_REQUEST_RISING_EDGE) < 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Failed to set up GPIO event\n");
        gpioTerminate();
        return EXIT_FAILURE;
    }

    if (gpioSetMode(VALVE_ENABLE_PIN, PI_OUTPUT) < 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Failed to set GPIO mode\n");
        gpioTerminate();
        return EXIT_FAILURE;
    }

    if (gpioSetMode(VALVE_PWM_PIN, PI_OUTPUT) < 0) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Failed to set GPIO mode\n");
        gpioTerminate();
        return EXIT_FAILURE;
    }

    gpioWrite(VALVE_ENABLE_PIN, 1);
    gpioSetPWMfrequency(VALVE_PWM_PIN, 1000);
    gpioSetPWMrange(VALVE_PWM_PIN, 255);

    clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC, &start_time);

    while (running) {
        clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC, &current_time);
        error = target_flow_rate - flow_rate;
        error_integral += error;
        error_derivative = error - last_error;
        last_error = error;
        pwm_value = (int)(kp * error + ki * error_integral + kd * error_derivative);
        pwm_value = (pwm_value < 0) ? 0 : (pwm_value > 255) ? 255 : pwm_value;
        gpioSetPWMdutycycle(VALVE_PWM_PIN, pwm_value);
        valve_position = (float)pwm_value / 255.0;
        printf("%ld,%f,%f\n", current_time.tv_sec * 1000 + current_time.tv_nsec / 1000000, flow_rate, valve_position);
        usleep(100000);
    }

    gpioSetPWMdutycycle(VALVE_PWM_PIN, 0);
    gpioWrite(VALVE_ENABLE_PIN, 0);
    gpioTerminate();

    return EXIT_SUCCESS;
}
```

This code sets up the GPIO lines, sets up the PWM for the solenoid valve, and then enters a loop where it calculates the error between the target flow rate and the current flow rate, and adjusts the PWM duty cycle accordingly. It also logs the current time, flow rate, and valve position to the console. The loop exits when the user sends a SIGINT or SIGTERM signal.

Please note that this code is a simplified version and does not include all the error handling and logging that you requested. It also assumes that the flow sensor pulses correspond to 0.1L of flow. You would need to adjust the code to fit your specific hardware and requirements.
Also, this code does not include the part of the code that writes the data to the CSV file. You would need to add that part of the code to write the data to the CSV file.

Here is a simple C program that fulfills the user's request:

```c
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <time.h>
#include <signal.h>
#include <libgpiod.h>

#define PIR_PIN 17
#define BUZZER_PIN 18
#define LOG_FILE "motion_log.txt"

static gpiod_chip *chip;
static gpiod_line *pir_line;
static gpiod_line *buzzer_line;
static FILE *log_file;

void cleanup() {
    gpiod_line_set_value(buzzer_line, 0);
    fclose(log_file);
    gpiod_line_release(pir_line);
    gpiod_line_release(buzzer_line);
    gpiod_chip_close(chip);
}

void signal_handler(int signum) {
    cleanup();
    exit(signum);
}

int main() {
    struct sigaction action;
    memset(&action, 0, sizeof(struct sigaction));
    action.sa_handler = signal_handler;
    sigaction(SIGINT, &action, NULL);
    sigaction(SIGTERM, &action, NULL);

    chip = gpiod_chip_open("/dev/gpiochip0");
    if (!chip) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Failed to open GPIO chip\n");
        return EXIT_FAILURE;
    }

    pir_line = gpiod_chip_get_line(chip, PIR_PIN);
    if (!pir_line) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Failed to get PIR line\n");
        goto cleanup;
    }

    buzzer_line = gpiod_chip_get_line(chip, BUZZER_PIN);
    if (!buzzer_line) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Failed to get buzzer line\n");
        goto cleanup;
    }

    log_file = fopen(LOG_FILE, "a");
    if (!log_file) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Failed to open log file\n");
        goto cleanup;
    }

    gpiod_line_request_input(pir_line, "PIR sensor");
    gpiod_line_request_output(buzzer_line, "Buzzer");

    while (1) {
        int value = gpiod_line_get_value(pir_line);
        if (value) {
            time_t now = time(NULL);
            struct tm *t = localtime(&now);
            char timestamp[20];
            strftime(timestamp, sizeof(timestamp), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S", t);
            fprintf(log_file, "%s\n", timestamp);

            gpiod_line_set_value(buzzer_line, 1);
            usleep(2000000);
            gpiod_line_set_value(buzzer_line, 0);
        }
    }

cleanup:
    cleanup();
    return EXIT_FAILURE;
}
```

This program opens the GPIO chip, gets the PIR and buzzer lines, and sets up signal handlers for SIGINT and SIGTERM. It then enters an infinite loop where it reads the PIR sensor value, logs the timestamp to the file if motion is detected, and buzzes for 2 seconds if motion is detected. The cleanup function is called on exit to release the GPIO resources and close the log file.

#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <signal.h>
#include <gpiod.h>

#define MOTOR1_PIN 17
#define MOTOR2_PIN 27
#define MOTOR1_CURRENT 60
#define MOTOR1_VOLTAGE 3
#define MOTOR1_DURATION 200
#define MOTOR2_CURRENT 60
#define MOTOR2_VOLTAGE 3
#define MOTOR2_DURATION 300

static void cleanup(gpiod_chip *chip, gpiod_line *line1, gpiod_line *line2) {
    gpiod_line_set_value(line1, 0);
    gpiod_line_set_value(line2, 0);
    gpiod_line_release(line1);
    gpiod_line_release(line2);
    gpiod_chip_close(chip);
}

static void handle_sigint(int signum) {
    printf("Received SIGINT, cleaning up...\n");
    cleanup(g_chip, g_line1, g_line2);
    exit(0);
}

static void handle_sigterm(int signum) {
    printf("Received SIGTERM, cleaning up...\n");
    cleanup(g_chip, g_line1, g_line2);
    exit(0);
}

int main() {
    struct gpiod_chip *chip;
    struct gpiod_line *line1, *line2;
    int ret;

    // Register signal handlers
    signal(SIGINT, handle_sigint);
    signal(SIGTERM, handle_sigterm);

    // Open GPIO chip
    chip = gpiod_chip_open("/dev/gpiochip0");
    if (!chip) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Failed to open GPIO chip\n");
        return EXIT_FAILURE;
    }

    // Request GPIO lines
    line1 = gpiod_chip_get_line(chip, MOTOR1_PIN);
    if (!line1) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Failed to get line %d\n", MOTOR1_PIN);
        gpiod_chip_close(chip);
        return EXIT_FAILURE;
    }

    line2 = gpiod_chip_get_line(chip, MOTOR2_PIN);
    if (!line2) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Failed to get line %d\n", MOTOR2_PIN);
        gpiod_line_release(line1);
        gpiod_chip_close(chip);
        return EXIT_FAILURE;
    }

    // Set GPIO lines to output
    ret = gpiod_line_request_output(line1, "haptic_motor1", 0);
    if (ret) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Failed to request line %d as output\n", MOTOR1_PIN);
        gpiod_line_release(line1);
        gpiod_line_release(line2);
        gpiod_chip_close(chip);
        return EXIT_FAILURE;
    }

    ret = gpiod_line_request_output(line2, "haptic_motor2", 0);
    if (ret) {
        fprintf(stderr, "Failed to request line %d as output\n", MOTOR2_PIN);
        gpiod_line_release(line1);
        gpiod_line_release(line2);
        gpiod_chip_close(chip);
        return EXIT_FAILURE;
    }

    g_chip = chip;
    g_line1 = line1;
    g_line2 = line2;

    while (1) {
        // Drive motor 1
        gpiod_line_set_value(line1, 1);
        usleep(MOTOR1_DURATION * 1000);
        gpiod_line_set_value(line1, 0);
        usleep((1000 - MOTOR1_DURATION) * 1000);

        // Drive motor 2
        gpiod_line_set_value(line2, 1);
        usleep(MOTOR2_DURATION * 1000);
        gpiod_line_set_value(line2, 0);
        usleep((1000 - MOTOR2_DURATION) * 1000);
    }

    return EXIT_SUCCESS;
}

Write a C program for a Raspberry Pi 3 Model B+ that uses an IR receiver such as the TSOP38238 connected to GPIO17 (BCM) to decode NEC infrared remote signals and report the decoded commands both to syslog and to an MQTT broker at localhost on port 1883 using the topic ir/decoded, publishing the command as a JSON object; the program must register an alert callback on the falling edge of the GPIO to capture pulse timings, interpret the NEC frame consisting of a 9 ms mark followed by a 4.5 ms space header, 560 µs marks for each bit, a 1690 µs space for logic‑1 and a 560 µs space for logic‑0, decode the full 32‑bit frame, validate the command against its inverted copy while allowing extended NEC frames that omit inverted‑address validation, check driver initialization and GPIO setup failures, guard against pulse‑buffer overflow, verify the NEC checksum, initialize the MQTT client once at startup and invoke the network loop in the main loop, and ensure clean release of all resources—including the driver, MQTT client, and syslog—when the process receives SIGINT or SIGTERM.

#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <string.h>
#include <unistd.h>
#include <fcntl.h>
#include <sys/ioctl.h>
#include <linux/i2c-dev.h>
#include <sys/socket.h>
#include <netinet/in.h>
#include <arpa/inet.h>
#include <signal.h>

#define BH1750_ADDRESS 0x23
#define BH1750_POWER_DOWN 0x00
#define BH1750_POWER_ON 0x01
#define BH1750_RESET 0x07
#define BH1750_CONTINUOUS_HIGH_RES_MODE 0x10
#define BH1750_CONVERSION_TIME 18000

int i2c_fd, udp_fd;
struct sockaddr_in udp_addr;
char buffer[256];

void signal_handler(int signum) {
    close(i2c_fd);
    close(udp_fd);
    exit(signum);
}

int main() {
    struct sigaction action;
    memset(&action, 0, sizeof(action));
    action.sa_handler = signal_handler;
    sigaction(SIGINT, &action, NULL);
    sigaction(SIGTERM, &action, NULL);

    if ((i2c_fd = open("/dev/i2c-1", O_RDWR)) < 0) {
        perror("Failed to open the i2c bus");
        return 1;
    }

    if (ioctl(i2c_fd, I2C_SLAVE, BH1750_ADDRESS) < 0) {
        perror("Failed to acquire bus access and/or talk to slave");
        return 1;
    }

    if (write(i2c_fd, &BH1750_POWER_ON, 1) < 0) {
        perror("Failed to write to i2c slave");
        return 1;
    }

    if (write(i2c_fd, &BH1750_RESET, 1) < 0) {
        perror("Failed to write to i2c slave");
        return 1;
    }

    if (write(i2c_fd, &BH1750_CONTINUOUS_HIGH_RES_MODE, 1) < 0) {
        perror("Failed to write to i2c slave");
        return 1;
    }

    if ((udp_fd = socket(AF_INET, SOCK_DGRAM, 0)) < 0) {
        perror("Failed to create socket");
        return 1;
    }

    memset(&udp_addr, 0, sizeof(udp_addr));
    udp_addr.sin_family = AF_INET;
    udp_addr.sin_port = htons(5000);
